doc.title: Ray Sherman interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 13, 1998

title: Winning Tommy Dorsey's Amateur Swing Contest at 15
summary: Back in Chicago he won the west coast broadcast of Dorsey's contest with 'Honeysuckle Rose' over George Barnes.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: No, I was just looking at my notes here.
Well that was when I was still in Chicago.
We can rewind. Let’s talk about that, and then I had something to ask you about in the service too.

Well that just reminded me, about the east coast and the west coast. It was Tommy Dorsey, he had the Raleigh and Kool Show that was called “The Amateur Swing Contest.” And it was a half hour show, and he would do it from whatever theater, you know they’re touring around playing theaters, whatever town they were in, they would do the show, and they would have auditions, you know a couple of weeks before the band was coming in each town that they were in. And so I auditioned for that and I got on the show. And the first, the east coast broadcast I think it was Barnes, is that the guitar player?
George Barns?

George Barns I think won it. He was older than me. I was 15 and I think he was about 18 or 19. But you were supposed to be amateur, you couldn’t belong to the union you know. And so he was eliminated and I won the west coast broadcast. Because in those days we should explain, there was no tape.
In the show—
In order to have it on at the same time in New York and at the same time in L.A., they had to do two broadcasts.
Right. And who were the judges of this?
The audience. The applause meter.
Oh, yeah, okay. Like Ted Mack.
Yeah, in a big theater, you know that makes sense.
Cool. © Fillius Jazz Archive -9-
Yeah. So on the second broadcast I got the most applause.
And you played “Honeysuckle Rose?”
I played “Honeysuckle Rose,” and I remember — are you familiar with the Dorsey Brothers record of “Honeysuckle Rose?”
A little bit.
Because I had memorized all the solos out of that, and I played a little bit of Tommy Dorsey’s solo, and I kept looking at him and he just didn’t react at all. Maybe he thought I was putting him on.
Maybe he didn’t recognize it.
Well he played [scats], which is another tune that he incorporated, so I thought it would be pretty obvious.
Well that’s neat. What did you get for that prize?
Oh, I won some money, I forgot how much. But the biggest thing is as a special thing my dad took me to the Black Hawk after the broadcast.
To the what?
To the Black Hawk to see the Bob Crosby band, which I’d never seen live. And he knew, God I loved this band, I listened every night on the radio.
He was probably pretty proud of you at that time. Neat.
Oh yeah. And he introduced me, of course they all knew him. And so I got to meet everybody.
Cool.
Yeah. I guess I remember that more than anything.
